Hi Sofie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then details and next steps: 

1) SOC 2 Type II report: yes — we completed a Type II for the period 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31. I attached the PDF for your review (Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06-01_2026-05-31.pdf).

2) Hosting / residency for EU/UK customers: Redwood Hosted customers who select EU residency are served from AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) by default; UK-only customers can be hosted in eu-west-2 (London) on request. Production request payloads and persistence are scoped to the customer region.

3) Operational pipelines: we separate customer request/payload data from telemetry. Request content and persistent customer artifacts remain in-customer-region storage; aggregated telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are sent to a central analytics pipeline (which currently resides in the US) for product health and capacity planning. We do not send raw customer PII or full request bodies to the analytics pipeline — we extract non-identifying metrics and apply hashing/aggregation. If you require zero cross-border transfer, we offer Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) that fully prevent cross-region exports.

4) Bridge letters / interim attestation: we can provide a brief bridge letter confirming the scope of the Type II and asserting that there have been no material changes to controls since the last audit. Typical turnaround for a signed bridge letter (standard wording) is 3–5 business days after Legal/Compliance approval. If you need custom language (e.g., specific to your internal policy), allow an extra 3–4 business days. I can route this to our compliance lead (Marissa) and legal (Kimberly) to prepare a draft.

I've cc'd Marissa (Compliance) and Karthik (your account executive) to coordinate delivery. For next steps: please confirm the exact assessment date in July and any mandatory evidence items (encryption at rest, key management, data retention, logging detail) you need; we'll compile the SOC2 PDF + evidence index and get a draft bridge letter started.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2025-06-01_2026-05-31.pdf

Kim/Naomi —

Priyom looped us in for a bridge letter request from Lumen Bank. They have an assessment in early July and appear to require: the SOC2 Type II PDF (attached by Priyom), a one-page bridge letter confirming audit window coverage and no material control changes, and an index of artifacts we can provide (key management screenshots, KMS integration proof, encryption at rest config, logging retention policy).

Draft wording I propose for the bridge letter (very short):

"Redwood Inference confirms that the SOC 2 Type II report for the period 2025-06-01 to 2026-05-31 accurately reflects the control environment for the Redwood Hosted service offering. Since the conclusion of the audit period, there have been no material changes to the controls relevant to security or availability for customers hosted in the EU region. Redwood hosts EU-resident customer data in AWS eu-west-1 (Ireland) unless a customer requests eu-west-2 (London) or a dedicated/private deployment. Aggregated product telemetry is processed in a central analytics environment; raw customer request payloads and PII are not transferred outside the customer-selected region. This letter is provided for the purpose of supporting Lumen Bank’s vendor assessment dated July 2026"

Can you confirm whether the "aggregated telemetry" line is acceptable as-is from a legal standpoint, or whether we need to hard-qualify with examples of data retained/transmitted? Also: we should attach the redwood-soc2-evidence-index.xlsx and a bridge_letter_draft.docx.

If you approve drafts, I'll have legal sign and return as a PDF (turnaround 1–3 days after sign-off).

Thanks,

Hi Sofie — thanks for the clear asks. Quick bullets and delivery plan: 

- Backups/snapshots: confirmed — for EU-hosted customers (eu-west-1 / eu-west-2) production backups and automated snapshots remain in the same region by default. We will include explicit language in the bridge letter.
- Logs / retention: standard retention for structured operational logs is 90 days; aggregated metrics are kept longer for trend analysis (360 days). Operational logs sent to the analytics pipeline are reduced to non-identifying metrics by default. We will provide the logging retention table in the evidence index.
- Dedicated/Private: typical lead time for a Dedicated reservation is 6–8 weeks (procurement + capacity allocation); Private VPC/on-prem discussions vary — we'll introduce you to our solutions engineering lead for scoping and a ballpark cost estimate.
